title: Introduction to Algorithms
author: Thomas H. Cormen, Charles E. Leiserson, Ronald L. Rivest, Clifford Stein
description: The definitive reference on algorithm design and analysis, covering sorting, graph algorithms, dynamic programming, and NP-completeness. Essential for every computer science student preparing for technical interviews or advanced research.

title: Computer Networks
author: Andrew S. Tanenbaum, David J. Wetherall
description: A comprehensive guide to networking concepts including the OSI model, TCP/IP, routing, Ethernet, wireless networks, and network security. Ideal for students pursuing networking, cloud computing, or systems engineering.

title: Operating System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Peter B. Galvin, Greg Gagne
description: Known as the 'Dinosaur Book', this text covers process management, memory management, file systems, and I/O. A cornerstone resource for understanding how modern operating systems function under the hood.

title: Database System Concepts
author: Abraham Silberschatz, Henry F. Korth, S. Sudarshan
description: Covers relational models, SQL, normalization, transaction management, concurrency control, and NoSQL databases. A must-read for students interested in data engineering, backend development, or database administration.

title: Clean Code: A Handbook of Agile Software Craftsmanship
author: Robert C. Martin
description: A transformative guide on writing readable, maintainable, and professional code. Covers naming conventions, functions, error handling, unit testing, and refactoring — essential reading for every aspiring software engineer.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
author: David Thomas, Andrew Hunt
description: A career-defining book on software development philosophy, covering topics from code reuse and testing to career growth and professional ethics. Highly recommended for students entering the software industry.

title: Computer Organization and Architecture
author: William Stallings
description: Covers the design of processors, memory hierarchies, instruction sets, I/O systems, and parallel architectures. Bridges the gap between hardware and software for computer engineering and CS students.

title: Compilers: Principles, Techniques, and Tools
author: Alfred V. Aho, Monica S. Lam, Ravi Sethi, Jeffrey D. Ullman
description: Widely known as the 'Dragon Book', this text covers lexical analysis, parsing, semantic analysis, code generation, and optimization. Fundamental for students in programming languages, compilers, and systems courses.

title: Design Patterns: Elements of Reusable Object-Oriented Software
author: Erich Gamma, Richard Helm, Ralph Johnson, John Vlissides
description: The legendary 'Gang of Four' book cataloguing 23 classic design patterns for object-oriented software. Indispensable for students learning software architecture, system design, and backend engineering.

title: Structure and Interpretation of Computer Programs
author: Harold Abelson, Gerald Jay Sussman, Julie Sussman
description: A foundational text in computer science education using Scheme to explore recursion, higher-order functions, interpreters, and program abstraction. Builds deep intuition for how programs execute and evolve.

title: Discrete Mathematics and Its Applications
author: Kenneth H. Rosen
description: Covers logic, set theory, combinatorics, graph theory, number theory, and proofs — the mathematical backbone of computer science. Essential reading for students in algorithms, cryptography, and formal methods.

title: Software Engineering
author: Ian Sommerville
description: A thorough survey of software engineering practices including agile methods, requirements engineering, software architecture, testing, and project management. Bridges theory and real-world development workflows.

title: Digital Design
author: M. Morris Mano, Michael D. Ciletti
description: Introduces the fundamentals of digital logic design including Boolean algebra, combinational and sequential circuits, flip-flops, registers, and HDL-based design. Core reading for electronics and computer engineering students.

title: Electronic Devices and Circuit Theory
author: Robert L. Boylestad, Louis Nashelsky
description: A comprehensive introduction to semiconductor devices, diodes, BJTs, FETs, amplifiers, and feedback circuits. Essential for first and second year electronics engineering students learning circuit analysis.

title: Microelectronic Circuits
author: Adel S. Sedra, Kenneth C. Smith
description: Covers MOSFET and BJT amplifiers, differential pairs, frequency response, feedback, and operational amplifiers in depth. The gold standard textbook for analog and mixed-signal circuit design courses.

title: Signals and Systems
author: Alan V. Oppenheim, Alan S. Willsky
description: A rigorous treatment of continuous and discrete-time signals, Fourier analysis, Laplace and Z-transforms, and LTI systems. Foundational for students in communications, control systems, and signal processing.

title: Communication Systems
author: Simon Haykin
description: Covers amplitude and angle modulation, pulse modulation, digital modulation schemes, and noise analysis. A thorough resource for students pursuing wireless communications, 5G, or signal processing careers.

title: VLSI Design
author: Neil H. E. Weste, David Harris
description: An in-depth guide to CMOS VLSI design, covering transistor physics, logic gates, datapath and memory design, timing, and power. Critical for students entering the semiconductor industry or chip design.

title: Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design
author: Constantine A. Balanis
description: The standard reference on antenna fundamentals, radiation patterns, dipoles, arrays, apertures, and microstrip antennas. Essential for students in RF engineering, satellite communications, and IoT system design.

title: Embedded Systems: Real-Time Operating Systems for ARM Cortex-M Microcontrollers
author: Jonathan W. Valvano
description: A hands-on guide to embedded programming on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, covering RTOS concepts, interfacing, ADC, UART, and real-time scheduling. Ideal for students working on IoT or embedded product development.

title: Microprocessors and Microcontrollers
author: N. Senthil Kumar, M. Saravanan, S. Jeevananthan
description: Covers 8085, 8086 microprocessors and 8051 microcontrollers including instruction sets, interfacing, interrupts, and peripheral devices. Widely used in undergraduate electronics and instrumentation courses.

title: Electromagnetic Field Theory Fundamentals
author: Bhag Singh Guru, Hüseyin R. Hızıroğlu
description: A rigorous yet accessible treatment of electrostatics, magnetostatics, Maxwell's equations, wave propagation, and transmission lines. Fundamental for electronics, telecommunications, and RF engineering students.

title: Power System Analysis
author: John J. Grainger, William D. Stevenson
description: The authoritative text on power system fundamentals including load flow, fault analysis, stability, and economic dispatch. A core reference for electrical engineering students specialising in power and energy systems.

title: Electrical Machinery
author: A. E. Fitzgerald, Charles Kingsley Jr., Stephen Umans
description: Covers the principles and analysis of transformers, DC machines, induction motors, and synchronous machines. A rigorous treatment suitable for undergraduate and postgraduate electrical engineering courses.

title: Modern Control Engineering
author: Katsuhiko Ogata
description: Covers classical and modern control theory including transfer functions, root locus, frequency response, Bode plots, state-space representation, and digital control. The standard text for control systems courses.

title: Power Electronics
author: Muhammad H. Rashid
description: Covers power semiconductor devices, rectifiers, inverters, choppers, and AC voltage controllers. Highly relevant for students in renewable energy, electric vehicles, and industrial drives.

title: Electric Circuits
author: James W. Nilsson, Susan A. Riedel
description: A foundational text on circuit analysis covering KVL, KCL, node and mesh analysis, Thevenin and Norton theorems, AC circuits, and Laplace transforms. Widely used in first-year electrical engineering courses.

title: Renewable Energy: Power for a Sustainable Future
author: Godfrey Boyle
description: Covers solar, wind, hydro, biomass, and tidal energy systems in technical depth. Highly relevant for students and practitioners pursuing sustainable energy, smart grids, and green engineering careers.

title: Digital Signal Processing
author: John G. Proakis, Dimitris G. Manolakis
description: A thorough treatment of discrete-time signals, DFT, FFT, IIR and FIR filter design, and multirate signal processing. Ideal for students entering audio, biomedical, radar, or communications signal processing fields.

title: High Voltage Engineering
author: M. S. Naidu, V. Kamaraju
description: Covers breakdown phenomena, insulating materials, surge phenomena, high voltage generation, and testing. An essential reference for students specialising in power transmission, transformer design, and utility engineering.

title: Instrumentation and Control Systems
author: William Bolton
description: Introduces sensors, transducers, data acquisition, PID controllers, and programmable logic controllers. Practical and accessible for students in instrumentation, industrial automation, and mechatronics.

title: Electric Power Systems: A First Course
author: Ned Mohan
description: A concise and modern introduction to electric power systems including generation, transmission, distribution, and the integration of renewable sources. Suitable for students entering the energy sector.

title: Engineering Thermodynamics
author: P. K. Nag
description: A comprehensive text on the laws of thermodynamics, properties of pure substances, gas power cycles, refrigeration, and psychrometrics. The standard Indian university textbook for mechanical engineering thermodynamics.

title: Fluid Mechanics
author: Frank M. White
description: Covers fluid statics, kinematics, energy equation, viscous flow, boundary layer theory, turbomachinery, and compressible flow. A rigorous and practical text widely used in mechanical and civil engineering programs.

title: Manufacturing Engineering and Technology
author: Serope Kalpakjian, Steven Schmid
description: An encyclopaedic reference covering casting, metal forming, machining, welding, polymer processing, and quality control. Prepares mechanical engineering students for careers in manufacturing, production, and industrial engineering.

title: Strength of Materials
author: R. K. Bansal
description: Covers stress, strain, shear force, bending moment diagrams, torsion, beam deflection, columns, and pressure vessels. A widely adopted text in Indian universities for mechanics of materials and solid mechanics courses.

title: Theory of Machines
author: S. S. Rattan
description: Covers kinematics and dynamics of mechanisms, gears, gear trains, cams, balancing, vibrations, and governors. Essential for mechanical engineering students studying machine design and dynamics.

title: Machine Design
author: V. B. Bhandari
description: Addresses design methodology, failure theories, fatigue, shafts, keys, bearings, gears, springs, and welded joints. The go-to reference for machine design courses in Indian engineering colleges.

title: Heat and Mass Transfer
author: R. C. Sachdeva
description: Covers conduction, convection, radiation, heat exchangers, and diffusion mass transfer. A practical and exam-oriented text aligned with the Indian mechanical engineering curriculum.

title: Robotics: Modelling, Planning and Control
author: Bruno Siciliano, Lorenzo Sciavicco, Luigi Villani, Giuseppe Oriolo
description: A rigorous treatment of robot kinematics, dynamics, trajectory planning, and control. Suitable for advanced mechanical and electronics engineering students pursuing robotics, automation, or mechatronics.

title: Internal Combustion Engines
author: V. Ganesan
description: Covers the thermodynamic cycles, combustion, carburetion, fuel injection, emissions, and performance of petrol and diesel engines. Relevant for students in automotive engineering and energy systems.

title: Mechanical Vibrations
author: Singiresu S. Rao
description: A comprehensive coverage of single and multi-degree-of-freedom vibration systems, damping, forced vibration, modal analysis, and vibration control. Core reading for mechanical and aerospace engineering students.

title: Chemical Reaction Engineering
author: Octave Levenspiel
description: The definitive textbook on chemical reactor analysis covering batch, CSTR, PFR, and non-ideal reactors, along with catalytic reactions and reaction kinetics. Essential for all chemical engineering students.

title: Transport Processes and Separation Process Principles
author: Christie J. Geankoplis, Allen Hersel, Daniel H. Lepek
description: Covers momentum, energy, and mass transfer alongside separation processes including distillation, absorption, liquid extraction, and membrane operations. A comprehensive and practical chemical engineering reference.

title: Introduction to Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics
author: J. M. Smith, H. C. Van Ness, M. M. Abbott
description: Covers PVT relations, thermodynamic properties, phase equilibria, chemical reaction equilibrium, and solution thermodynamics. A core text for chemical engineering thermodynamics courses at the undergraduate level.

title: Process Dynamics and Control
author: Dale E. Seborg, Thomas F. Edgar, Duncan A. Mellichamp, Francis J. Doyle III
description: A rigorous treatment of dynamic modelling, Laplace transforms, PID control, frequency response, and advanced process control for chemical plants. Essential for process control and automation courses.

title: Principles of Mass Transfer and Separation Processes
author: Binay K. Dutta
description: Covers diffusion, convective mass transfer, gas absorption, distillation, and extraction with solved examples tailored for Indian university curricula. Clear and systematic presentation for chemical engineering students.

title: Chemical Engineering Design
author: Gavin Towler, Ray Sinnott
description: Provides a systematic methodology for process design, equipment selection, cost estimation, safety, and sustainability assessment. Invaluable for final year chemical engineering students undertaking plant design projects.

title: Fluid Mechanics and Machinery
author: C. S. P. Ojha, R. Berndtsson, P. N. Chandramouli
description: Covers fluid properties, Bernoulli's equation, pipe flow, pumps, compressors, and hydraulic turbines with emphasis on chemical plant applications. Suitable for chemical and environmental engineering students.

title: Biochemical Engineering
author: James E. Bailey, David F. Ollis
description: A landmark text covering enzyme kinetics, microbial growth, bioreactor design, and downstream processing. Essential for students at the intersection of chemical engineering and biotechnology.

title: Coulson and Richardson's Chemical Engineering Volume 1
author: J. M. Coulson, J. F. Richardson
description: A comprehensive reference on fluid flow, heat transfer, and mass transfer for chemical engineers. Part of the definitive Coulson & Richardson series used in chemical engineering programs worldwide.

title: Environmental Engineering
author: Peavy, Rowe, Tchobanoglous
description: Covers water supply, wastewater treatment, air pollution control, solid waste management, and noise pollution. Foundational for students pursuing environmental, chemical, or civil engineering with a sustainability focus.

title: Structural Analysis
author: R. C. Hibbeler
description: Covers equilibrium, trusses, beams, frames, virtual work, influence lines, and the stiffness matrix method. A clear, example-rich text that is the standard in undergraduate structural analysis courses.

title: Geotechnical Engineering
author: Braja M. Das
description: Covers soil classification, compaction, permeability, consolidation, shear strength, bearing capacity, slope stability, and retaining walls. The leading geotechnical engineering textbook for civil engineering undergraduates.

title: Surveying
author: B. C. Punmia
description: A complete reference on chain surveying, compass, theodolite, levelling, plane table, tacheometry, curves, and remote sensing. The definitive surveying text used across Indian civil engineering programmes.

title: Reinforced Concrete Design
author: Chu-Kia Wang, Charles Salmon, Jose Pincheira
description: Covers design of beams, slabs, columns, footings, retaining walls, and connections per ACI codes. A thorough text for students and professionals working in structural and construction engineering.

title: Transportation Engineering
author: C. S. Papacostas, P. D. Prevedouros
description: Covers highway engineering, traffic flow theory, geometric design, pavement design, and transportation planning. Essential for civil engineering students pursuing infrastructure and urban planning specialisations.

title: Environmental Engineering
author: Howard S. Peavy, Donald R. Rowe
description: Covers water and wastewater treatment, solid waste management, and air quality control from a civil engineering design perspective. Relevant for students working on municipal infrastructure and environmental compliance.

title: Fluid Mechanics for Civil Engineers
author: N. B. Webber
description: A civil engineering-focused treatment of fluid statics, open channel flow, pipe networks, and hydraulic structures. A concise and practical reference for students in water resources and hydraulics courses.

title: Building Construction
author: Sushil Kumar
description: Covers foundations, masonry, concrete construction, formwork, roofing, plastering, and finishing. Extensively used by civil engineering students and practising construction engineers in India.

title: Hydrology and Water Resources Engineering
author: S. K. Garg
description: A detailed treatment of precipitation, runoff, groundwater, floods, reservoirs, and irrigation systems. A standard reference for civil engineering students specialising in water resources or irrigation engineering.

title: Design of Steel Structures
author: L. S. Negi
description: Covers properties of structural steel, design of tension and compression members, beams, connections, and industrial buildings per IS codes. Aligned with the Indian curriculum for structural steel design courses.

title: Advanced Engineering Mathematics
author: Erwin Kreyszig
description: A comprehensive resource covering ODEs, PDEs, linear algebra, vector calculus, Fourier analysis, complex analysis, and probability. The single most important mathematics reference for all engineering disciplines.

title: Linear Algebra and Its Applications
author: Gilbert Strang
description: Covers vector spaces, matrix factorizations, eigenvalues, linear transformations, and applications to engineering and data science. Gilbert Strang's approachable style makes this a favourite among students and self-learners.

title: Probability and Statistics for Engineering and the Sciences
author: Jay L. Devore
description: Covers probability theory, random variables, distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and quality control with engineering applications. A standard text for applied statistics courses in engineering programs.

title: Numerical Methods for Engineers
author: Steven C. Chapra, Raymond P. Canale
description: Covers root finding, numerical integration, ODEs, linear systems, interpolation, and optimisation with MATLAB examples. Practical and problem-focused, suitable for all engineering disciplines requiring computational methods.

title: Calculus: Early Transcendentals
author: James Stewart
description: The world's most widely used calculus textbook, covering limits, derivatives, integrals, series, and multivariable calculus with clear explanations and rich problem sets. Foundational for all first-year engineering students.

title: Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach
author: Stuart Russell, Peter Norvig
description: The definitive AI textbook covering search, planning, knowledge representation, probabilistic reasoning, machine learning, perception, and natural language processing. Essential reading for any student pursuing AI or ML.

title: Deep Learning
author: Ian Goodfellow, Yoshua Bengio, Aaron Courville
description: A comprehensive treatment of neural networks, backpropagation, regularisation, CNNs, RNNs, autoencoders, and generative models. The theoretical bible for students entering deep learning research or applied AI.

title: Pattern Recognition and Machine Learning
author: Christopher M. Bishop
description: Covers probabilistic graphical models, Bayesian methods, kernel methods, neural networks, and mixture models from first principles. A rigorous and mathematically deep text for graduate-level machine learning.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
author: Richard S. Sutton, Andrew G. Barto
description: The definitive textbook on reinforcement learning covering Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, temporal difference learning, Q-learning, and policy gradient methods. Essential for students in AI, robotics, and game AI.

title: Natural Language Processing with Transformers
author: Lewis Tunstall, Leandro von Werra, Thomas Wolf
description: A hands-on guide to modern NLP using Hugging Face Transformers, covering BERT, GPT, T5, question answering, summarisation, and named entity recognition. Highly practical for students building language model applications.

title: Hands-On Machine Learning with Scikit-Learn, Keras and TensorFlow
author: Aurélien Géron
description: A practical end-to-end guide covering regression, classification, SVMs, decision trees, ensemble methods, neural networks, CNNs, RNNs, and autoencoders with Python. The most popular ML book for practitioners and students.

title: Python for Data Analysis
author: Wes McKinney
description: Written by the creator of Pandas, this book covers NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, and data wrangling techniques. The essential Python reference for data science, analytics, and quantitative engineering students.

title: The Elements of Statistical Learning
author: Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani, Jerome Friedman
description: A mathematically rigorous survey of supervised and unsupervised learning including regression, SVMs, random forests, boosting, and neural networks. The definitive statistical ML reference for advanced students and researchers.

title: Data Science from Scratch
author: Joel Grus
description: Builds core data science algorithms from scratch in Python — including k-NN, decision trees, neural networks, and recommender systems — giving students deep intuition for how modern ML tools actually work.

title: Big Data: A Revolution That Will Transform How We Live, Work, and Think
author: Viktor Mayer-Schönberger, Kenneth Cukier
description: An accessible and thought-provoking exploration of how massive datasets are reshaping science, business, health, and governance. Valuable context-setting reading for any student entering data engineering or analytics.

title: Principles of Management
author: Harold Koontz, Heinz Weihrich
description: Covers planning, organising, staffing, directing, and controlling within organisations. A widely adopted management text that gives engineering students a strong foundation in business and leadership principles.

title: Engineering Management: Meeting the Global Challenges
author: Burton Dean, Bonnie Ulrich, Ernest Forman
description: Bridges technical and managerial competencies covering project management, strategic planning, decision analysis, and innovation management. Tailored for engineers stepping into leadership or product management roles.

title: Project Management: The Managerial Process
author: Erik W. Larson, Clifford F. Gray
description: A comprehensive guide to project scope, scheduling, cost estimation, risk management, agile methods, and project closure. Highly practical for engineering students involved in technical project management and consultancy.

title: Operations Management
author: William J. Stevenson
description: Covers forecasting, supply chain management, capacity planning, inventory control, lean production, and quality management. Bridges engineering and business for students pursuing operations or industrial engineering.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
description: Introduces the Build-Measure-Learn feedback loop, minimum viable products, and validated learning as tools for building startups under uncertainty. A must-read for any engineering student considering founding a company.

title: Zero to One: Notes on Startups, or How to Build the Future
author: Peter Thiel, Blake Masters
description: Peter Thiel's contrarian philosophy on building breakthrough technology companies, creating monopolies, and thinking boldly about the future. Widely read by student founders and aspiring technology entrepreneurs.

title: The Startup Owner's Manual
author: Steve Blank, Bob Dorf
description: A step-by-step guide to customer discovery, customer validation, and business model design. Foundational for engineering students applying lean startup methodologies to build tech ventures or college projects.

title: Start with Why
author: Simon Sinek
description: Explores why purpose-driven leadership and communication inspire loyalty, innovation, and long-lasting organisations. Valuable for student entrepreneurs and engineers interested in building mission-driven products and teams.

title: Good to Great
author: Jim Collins
description: Analyses the traits and disciplines that allowed certain companies to make the leap from good performance to exceptional and sustained results. Recommended for engineering students interested in organisational strategy and leadership.

title: The Innovator's Dilemma
author: Clayton M. Christensen
description: Introduces disruptive innovation theory and explains why established companies fail when confronted by new entrants. Essential reading for engineering students thinking about technology commercialisation and market disruption.

title: Storytelling with Data
author: Cole Nussbaumer Knaflic
description: Teaches how to design effective data visualisations and communicate insights clearly to non-technical audiences. Useful for data science, business analytics, and engineering students presenting project results or dashboards.

title: Generative Deep Learning
author: David Foster
description: Covers generative adversarial networks, variational autoencoders, diffusion models, transformers, and large language models with hands-on Keras examples. Essential for students exploring creative AI, image synthesis, and LLM development.

title: The McKinsey Way
author: Ethan M. Rasiel
description: Reveals McKinsey's structured problem-solving frameworks, hypothesis-driven analysis, and client communication techniques. Popular among engineering students aspiring to management consulting or strategic roles in tech companies.

title: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications
author: Richard Szeliski
description: A comprehensive survey of image formation, feature detection, segmentation, stereo vision, 3D reconstruction, and deep learning for vision. Suitable for students in robotics, autonomous systems, and applied AI research.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
author: Martin Kleppmann
description: Explores the principles behind scalable, reliable, and maintainable data systems covering replication, partitioning, transactions, stream processing, and batch processing. Essential for students interested in data engineering and backend systems.

title: Hooked: How to Build Habit-Forming Products
author: Nir Eyal
description: Describes the Hook Model — trigger, action, reward, investment — behind addictive consumer products. Valuable for student founders and engineering students building mobile apps or user-facing products.

title: Complex Variables and Applications
author: James Ward Brown, Ruel V. Churchill
description: Covers complex numbers, analytic functions, contour integration, Laurent series, residues, and conformal mappings. Fundamental for electrical engineering, fluid mechanics, and applied mathematics students.

title: Computer Security: Art and Science
author: Matt Bishop
description: A thorough treatment of security principles, access control, cryptography, network security, intrusion detection, and malware analysis. Highly relevant for students pursuing cybersecurity, ethical hacking, or cloud security careers.

title: Speech and Language Processing
author: Daniel Jurafsky, James H. Martin
description: The definitive NLP reference covering text classification, sequence models, neural networks, transformers, machine translation, sentiment analysis, and dialogue systems. Essential for students pursuing language AI or conversational AI research.

title: Introduction to Statistical Learning with Applications in R
author: Gareth James, Daniela Witten, Trevor Hastie, Robert Tibshirani
description: A gentler introduction to statistical learning methods including regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree methods, SVMs, and clustering. An accessible entry point to machine learning for students with a statistics background.

title: Strategic Management: Concepts and Cases
author: Fred R. David, Forest R. David
description: Covers SWOT, competitive analysis, strategy formulation and implementation through real-world case studies. Useful for engineering students interested in technology management, product strategy, or business development.

title: Sprint: How to Solve Big Problems and Test New Ideas in Just Five Days
author: Jake Knapp, John Zeratsky, Braden Kowitz
description: Describes Google Ventures' five-day design sprint methodology for rapidly prototyping and testing product ideas. Highly practical for engineering students in hackathons, capstone projects, or product development roles.

title: Graph Theory
author: Frank Harary
description: A classic rigorous treatment of graph theory covering trees, connectivity, matchings, colourings, and planar graphs. Valuable for computer science and mathematics students studying algorithms, networks, and combinatorics.
